narrative.overview: The Protect Diversity visual system is built on a single conviction: information density is a feature, not a flaw. Where most skincare brands use sparse elegance to signal luxury, Protect Diversity uses precision and transparency to signal trust. The palette is grounded in Mexican earth: warm cacao as the dominant ink, terracota as the voice of conviction, crema as the surface that breathes. This is not a cream-and-minimalism aesthetic by default — it is a deliberate palette that evokes the skin tones and regional materials of Mexico.
keyCharacteristics: Serif display (Fraunces) paired with humanist sans (Manrope) — confidence + legibility
Pill-shaped controls contrast with editorial typography for clear affordance hierarchy
Terracota is the voice color — used for emphasis, not decoration
Cacao as both ink and primary surface creates tonal cohesion across dark sections
No shadows on cards at rest; depth comes from tonal contrast between surface levels

rules.name: La Regla Terracota
rules.body: Terracota (#C45A2C) appears on ≤15% of any screen. Headlines in terracota must be italic Fraunces; never upright roman, never Manrope.

rules.name: La Regla de Superficie
rules.body: Pages have three surface levels: crema (base), crema-profunda (raised), blanco (elevated). Shadows are not used to create depth — surface color does that work.

rules.name: La Regla Fraunces
rules.body: Every terracota text on the page is Fraunces italic. The combination of color + weight + style is the brand's accent voice — breaking any part of the triplet dilutes the signal.

rules.name: La Regla del Techo
rules.body: Display headings: clamp max is 4.5rem (72px). Letter-spacing floor is -0.025em. Above these values the page shouts, not designs.

rules.name: La Regla Plana
rules.body: Every surface is flat at rest. If a card has a shadow before the user does anything, remove it. Elevation is a response to interaction, not a decorative default.

dos: Do use Fraunces italic in terracota for emphasis — preserve the triplet (Fraunces + italic + terracota) as a unit
Do use tonal surface depth (crema → crema-profunda → blanco) to create hierarchy
Do gate all hover animations behind @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)
Do include specific ingredient names, percentages, and certifications in product copy
Do use text-wrap: balance on H1–H2 and text-wrap: pretty on prose
Do keep reveal animations on content that is already visible at rest
Do use salvia for trust signals, eco certifications, and confirmation states
Do use pill-radius (999px) on all interactive controls — buttons, pills, badges
donts: Don't use luxury-brand aesthetics (La Mer, Tatcha-style): aspirational staging, gold accents, exclusion-coded language
Don't use clinical-cold pharmacy aesthetics (sterile blue-white, hospital-style grids)
Don't use cream/sand/beige as a second neutral — the crema palette is specific and brand-tied
Don't add eyebrow labels above every section — use them selectively for sections with real semantic purpose
Don't pair a border: 1px solid with a large box-shadow on the same card at rest
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text) — emphasis is through Fraunces weight, italic, or terracota
Don't use border-radius above 16px on cards
Don't animate from opacity: 0 initial states that aren't already visible at rest
Don't exceed the display clamp ceiling of 4.5rem or tighten letter-spacing below -0.025em
Don't use transition: all — specify exact properties with explicit durations and ease-out curves
